summary: Separated real Linux root-ownership transaction fixtures from unprivileged deployment checks. Affected CI preserves ordinary-user execution and runs only the selected root fixtures in an additional disposable hosted job, using the OS Python interpreter and a clean environment. No production deployment behavior or ownership rule was weakened.
changes: Moved the real ownership-dependent control-update, HTTPS transaction, management-boundary and release-reuse classes into four tests/deploy/root/test_*.py files. Ordinary interface/rendering/preflight/installation checks remain in their original unprivileged group. The two HTTPS rendering tests moved from test_deployment.py to the ordinary test_https.py, preserving all test cases.

Added an explicit deploy-root impact group. Changes to either half of each split fixture select both identity groups; missing companions require coverage review. The all selection still includes both groups, and workflow changes select deployment identity regressions.

Added a separate ubuntu-24.04 CI job guarded by RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT=github-hosted. It receives only the exact selected root-file list from the impact plan, checks bounded unique ordinary paths, and executes those files with /usr/bin/sudo and OS-installed /usr/bin/python3 -I -B in an empty environment with an isolated temporary home. Checkout and all npm/pnpm installation remain unprivileged; the root job installs no dependencies.

Preserved nonzero missing-interpreter, empty-file and skipped-test results. Added regression checks proving nested root fixtures remain in targeted/full inventories and verifying identity-group selection. The full-audit gate was not changed; run-tests.mjs already supports the nested paths.
Updated deployment test instructions and qualified pre-split Windows counts as historical evidence.

validation.purpose: Verified that Linux/root absence remains a nonzero coverage gap rather than a pass.

validation.result: All 12 deployment test files and the exact CI root Python heredoc compile without writing bytecode; scripts/select-tests.mjs passes node --check.

validation.serviceSafety: Parent verified all six existing service PIDs and InvocationIDs were unchanged. The root driver was extracted verbatim from the workflow heredoc.
validation.initialHarnessFailure: The first isolated validation tar omitted package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and pnpm-workspace.yaml, causing two source-input tests to error while the other 65 ordinary tests passed. Adding those three unchanged source inputs produced the final 67/67 result. The ignored packaging helper was corrected; no product/test code change was required for this harness error.

limits: The actual GitHub hosted workflow was not dispatched. Its exact root Python driver and selected files were executed on the isolated Linux host; checkout/job-expression behavior remains a static workflow review.
The Linux execution and unchanged-service observations were performed and reported by the coordinating root agent, with the separate linked Linux evidence artifact.
No full repository suite was run, no online deployment/migration occurred, and no paid model or external MCP operation was performed.
This is a targeted fix/verification record for R2-DEPLOY-001, not an independent clean full-repository audit and not authorization to bypass the three-round gate.
